ideal.reply: A quest is not a checklist. It is the specification of one intention you care about, plus a plan to carry it out, so Quest asks where you want to end up, why it matters, where you are now and what you have already tried. ideal.reply: ESOI stands for Evolvable Structure that Optimizes Intent. In plain words, Quest treats your goal of cutting your anxiety in half as one intention: it writes down the end state you want, what is in the way and what you have already tried, and candidate strategies, and it keeps adjusting that structure as you learn what works. Experiments are how you learn that for yourself. You ask a research question, such as which morning routine lowers your anxiety most, look at what existing evidence says, then test it in your own life by tracking a habit or a collection, and Analyze my data shows what your results suggest. So the plan is not fixed: your own evidence improves it.

An external environment task is a deep run on one of your team's connected runners, for work only that machine can do, such as checking server logs. You do not need an external environment to have tasks: a Quest operation or a web search is a task like any other.

ideal.reply: A workflow shows who does what, and when, as a diagram: steps joined by arrows. Each step is run by a person on your team or by one of your AI reps, and says what needs to happen and by when, and Quest watches whether it happened so a missed step shows up as a risk. To create one for your weekly review, open the menu, expand AI Productivity, tap Workflows, then tap New workflow, name it, choose your team, and pick Describe it and let AI draft it. Say what the review is for and who is involved, ask for changes if the draft is off, and nothing runs until you choose Create workflow. Workflows are part of the paid plans.

ideal.reply: An AI rep is your own AI counterpart in Quest: the version of Quest AI that acts as you, carrying your context, working in your voice and running work on your behalf. You always have one default rep, which represents you to your teammates and conducts a chat or runs a task when no other rep is chosen. You can create more for different areas, for example a research rep and a writing rep, each with a name, a short description and a persona that says how it should respond as you. When a teammate brings your rep into a chat or hands it a task, it answers grounded in your context and preferences.

ideal.reply: Two papers the search found point the same way. A systematic review of 14 studies (Author A and others, 2021, Journal of Demo Sports Medicine, DOI 10.5555/sci.demo.cycling-review) found cycling kept aerobic capacity in most of them. A small trial of 38 adults after a knee ligament strain (Author D and Author E, 2019, DOI 10.5555/sci.demo.knee-trial) found stationary cycling three times a week kept fitness close to baseline. I read only the abstracts, not the full text, so treat this as a suggestion rather than a conclusion: the review says study quality was mixed and the trial was small and lasted eight weeks. Your physio's say-so on pain and load still comes first.
